Diagnosis:
The test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477` fails due to an OutOfMemoryError when using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes. The pattern being tested is:

```java
String pattern = "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!";
```

The failure is linked to how ExtendedMessageFormat processes patterns with single quotes and custom format registries.

Looking at the ExtendedMessageFormat constructors, the constructor with pattern and registry calls `applyPattern`, which is where pattern parsing happens with registry support.

The `applyPattern` method processes the pattern character by character. It handles quoted strings via the `appendQuotedString` method when encountering a quote character ('). The pattern mentioned contains multiple single quotes, including escaped quotes (two consecutive single quotes).

`appendQuotedString` attempts to deal with quotes and escaped quotes. When the pattern substring at the current position starts with an escaped quote (`''`), it appends a single quote and advances the position by the length of the escaped quote. This appears correct.

The problem arises when the format registry is non-null, so the pattern will be scanned for format elements: `{0,lower}` in the test pattern. The code tries to parse and extract the argument index and format description.

The root cause is likely that the parsing logic in `applyPattern` and the helper methods incorrectly handles nested or multiple single quotes with custom registry leading to infinite loops or excessive memory consumption, causing OutOfMemoryError.

The test pattern contains `'test'`, a quoted string after the `{0,lower}` format; if the parsing doesn't correctly skip quoted strings or handle them differently with custom registry, it could repeatedly parse the same section or create large buffers.

In summary, the bug stems from ExtendedMessageFormat's improper handling of single quotes and format elements when a custom format registry is set, causing unbound memory usage when the input pattern includes quoted substrings. The infinite or uncontrolled recursion or looping likely occurs inside `applyPattern` or `appendQuotedString` when processing escaped quotes and custom formats together.

Recent bug reports do not specifically relate to this issue and can be ignored for this diagnosis.

Hence, the issue can be traced to the combination of `ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(String)` and `ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(String, ParsePosition, StringBuffer, boolean)` methods not correctly handling patterns with single quotes and custom format registry.

Next, I will recommend which methods to fix.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String,java.text.ParsePosition,java.lang.StringBuffer,boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
